title: The Value a Catering Order Stands At When Notice of Cancellation Is Given
content:
## The quantity

The value standing on a catering order at the moment the client gives notice of cancellation is worked out afresh from the entries the order carries rather than read off the quotation it was first placed at. The order is one placed under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement.

## The entries the order carries

The entries taken into account are those standing against the order in the 12 months ending on the day notice is given: the entry that placed the order, which records the value it was placed at, the guest count it stood on and the day it was to be served; and any amendment entry, which records the value and the guest count it left the order on and the day the amendment was asked for.

## The value selected

The value the order was placed at stands.

## The free reduction band

The free reduction band standing on an order is the band printed against the catering service level.

## The concessions

No trading discount is taken on the value standing. No programme concession is taken on the value standing.

## Putting the two together

The trading discount taken and the programme concession are first added into one total concession rate, and the value selected above is reduced once by that total rate; the two do not act successively, and the result is rounded to two decimal places only at the end.

## Worked illustration on hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical order placed at 1250.00 USD on 40 guests, with notice of cancellation given eight days before the service day.

| Component | Hypothetical figure |
| --- | --- |
| Value selected | 1250.00 USD |
| Trading discount taken | 0.0 per cent |
| Programme concession | 0.0 per cent |
| Total concession rate | 0.0 per cent |
| Value standing at notice | 1250.00 USD |

The trading discount taken and the programme concession are gathered into the total concession rate before anything is reduced, and that single total rate is applied once to the value selected; neither rate is applied to a value already reduced by the other, and the figure is taken to two decimal places once, at the end.
